---
title: "xenium_nb — sample summary"
subtitle: "Per-cell QC by cluster, one sample per section"
# Pin the kernel by name, as cluster_report.qmd does. Apptainer bind-mounts $HOME, so
# kernelspecs from ~/.local/share/jupyter/kernels shadow the container's own — quarto's
# default "python3" then resolves to a host env missing the pipeline's packages, and
# every cell fails at import under `error: true` while the render still exits 0.
jupyter: python_spatial
format:
  pptx:
    reference-doc: ouhsc_ppt_template.pptx
    # `#` becomes a Section Header slide, `##` a Title-and-Content slide. Without
    # this pandoc infers the level from the headings present, so adding the first
    # `#` would silently demote every `##` to a bullet.
    slide-level: 2
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  # Keep rendering when a cell raises: one sample's panel erroring leaves an error slide
  # in its own section instead of taking the whole deck down. The cost is that a
  # genuinely broken cell yields an error slide and an exit code of 0 — read the slides,
  # not just the exit status.
  error: true
---

```{python}
# | tags: [setup]
import gc
import traceback
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import matplotlib.patheffects as patheffects
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.sparse as sp
import zarr
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import leaves_list, linkage
from scipy.spatial.distance import squareform
from scipy.stats import rankdata

# The reference template is 16:9 at 10 x 5.625in; leave room for a slide title.
FIGSIZE = (9.0, 4.3)

# Every clustered zarr is staged into this notebook's working directory by the Nextflow
# process, so globbing is the whole input contract — no params to pass or drift. These
# are cluster_sdata's zarrs, not create_sdata's: they carry the leiden_res_* columns,
# and their cells are already past the min_counts cut.
ZARRS = sorted(Path(".").glob("*.zarr"))
if not ZARRS:
    raise FileNotFoundError("No .zarr directories staged next to the notebook.")

# The resolution each sample's clusters are taken at unless its row in
# chosen_resolutions.csv says otherwise. A cohort-wide starting point, not a claim that
# 0.5 is right for any particular sample — the right resolution is a judgement made by
# reading cluster_report, and this is what the deck splits on until that judgement exists.
DEFAULT_RESOLUTION = 0.5

# The per-sample resolution table, staged flat beside the zarrs by the same
# staging-is-the-contract rule. Its rows are OVERRIDES on DEFAULT_RESOLUTION, not a
# required entry per sample: a cohort renders with no rows at all, and a sample gets its
# own resolution the moment one is written for it. Optional as a file too — if it is
# absent every sample simply takes the default.
RESOLUTIONS_CSV = Path("chosen_resolutions.csv")

# obs columns holding the five Xenium control/codeword counters. Summed into a single
# negative-control fraction; each one alone is too sparse to read per cell.
CONTROL_COLS = [
    "control_probe_counts",
    "genomic_control_counts",
    "control_codeword_counts",
    "unassigned_codeword_counts",
    "deprecated_codeword_counts",
]


def load_obs(path):
    """Read one zarr's obs and UMAP coords without pulling X into memory.

    ad.io.read_elem on the table's obs/obsm groups reads those alone — the count matrix
    stays on disk. spatialdata.read_zarr would instead materialize every image and the
    full X for each sample, and this deck only ever needs obs and the embedding.
    """
    store = zarr.open(f"{path}/tables/table", mode="r")
    df = ad.io.read_elem(store["obs"])

    umap = ad.io.read_elem(store["obsm"]["X_umap"])
    df["umap_1"] = umap[:, 0]
    df["umap_2"] = umap[:, 1]

    # Negative-control fraction, computed here rather than read from obs. It cannot use
    # total_counts: create_sdata's total_counts is transcripts + all five counters, but
    # cluster_sdata's calculate_qc_metrics overwrites it with X.sum(axis=1) — so the
    # column means different things before and after clustering. transcript_counts is
    # the one that always equals the row sum of X, so the denominator is rebuilt from it.
    present = [c for c in CONTROL_COLS if c in df.columns]
    if present:
        controls = df[present].sum(axis=1)
        df["pct_control"] = 100 * controls / (df["transcript_counts"] + controls)

    return df


def resolution_columns(df):
    """The sweep's leiden columns, ordered by resolution rather than by string.

    Discovered from obs rather than hardcoded: --resolutions is a pipeline param, so the
    set of columns is whatever the run that produced these zarrs chose. Sorting on the
    float matters — a plain sort puts leiden_res_1.00 before leiden_res_0.20.
    """
    cols = [c for c in df.columns if c.startswith("leiden_res_")]
    return sorted(cols, key=lambda c: float(c.removeprefix("leiden_res_")))


# sample -> overriding resolution, as the float the CSV records. Read once here so a
# malformed table fails the whole deck rather than every per-sample slide separately.
# Samples absent from it (or from a missing file) fall back to DEFAULT_RESOLUTION.
OVERRIDES = {}
if RESOLUTIONS_CSV.exists():
    chosen = pd.read_csv(RESOLUTIONS_CSV)
    missing_cols = {"sample", "resolution"} - set(chosen.columns)
    if missing_cols:
        raise ValueError(f"chosen_resolutions.csv missing column(s): {sorted(missing_cols)}")
    OVERRIDES = dict(zip(chosen["sample"].astype(str), chosen["resolution"].astype(float)))
```

```{python}
# Load the cohort. Each zarr's obs is read once, up front, and kept: obs alone is ~10-50 MB
# per sample against the multi-GB images and X that stay on disk, so the whole cohort fits
# in memory and every slide below reads from these frames rather than reopening a store.
samples = {}
# sample -> the zarr it came from, kept because the centroid cell below has to reopen the
# store for X. The staged path is not derivable from the sample id: cluster_sdata*
# publishes every sample's output as clustered.zarr, so the names are sample1, sample2, …
zarr_paths = {}

for path in ZARRS:
    df = load_obs(path)
    # obs["sample"] is written by create_sdata and survives clustering, so the sample id
    # comes from the object rather than the staged path — which is a meaningless
    # sample1.zarr, since cluster_sdata* publishes every sample's output as clustered.zarr.
    sample = str(df["sample"].iloc[0])
    samples[sample] = df
    zarr_paths[sample] = path

SAMPLES = sorted(samples)

# sample -> the resolution this deck splits it at: its override if it has one, the
# cohort default otherwise.
CHOSEN = {sample: OVERRIDES.get(sample, DEFAULT_RESOLUTION) for sample in SAMPLES}

# Whichever resolution a sample lands on, it must name a leiden column that exists —
# a default of 0.5 is no help if the run that produced these zarrs swept 0.6 to 1.0.
# Checked here for the whole cohort rather than per slide: splitting on a resolution the
# zarr does not carry is a hard error, and finding out about every such sample at once
# beats one render per fix.
problems = []
for sample in SAMPLES:
    key = f"leiden_res_{CHOSEN[sample]:.2f}"
    if key not in samples[sample].columns:
        available = ", ".join(resolution_columns(samples[sample])) or "none"
        source = "override" if sample in OVERRIDES else "default"
        problems.append(
            f"{sample}: {source} resolution {CHOSEN[sample]:g} -> '{key}' not in obs. Available: {available}"
        )
if problems:
    raise ValueError(
        "No matching leiden column for:\n  " + "\n  ".join(problems)
        + "\n\nSet a per-sample resolution in chosen_resolutions.csv, or change DEFAULT_RESOLUTION."
    )
```

```{python}
# The per-cell QC columns each sample's panel shows, as (obs column, axis label, log).
# Counts and areas are strictly positive and heavily right-skewed, so they are shown on a
# log scale; pct_control is a bounded percentage that is exactly 0 for most cells, which
# a log scale would drop silently, so it stays linear.
QC_COLUMNS = [
    ("transcript_counts", "Transcripts", True),
    ("n_genes_by_counts", "Genes", True),
    ("cell_area", "Cell area (µm²)", True),
    ("pct_control", "Negative control %", False),
]


def size_ranked(labels):
    """Leiden labels ordered largest cluster first, for renumbering to 1..n.

    Leiden's own ids carry no meaning across samples — they are assignment order, so
    cluster 3 in one sample has nothing to do with cluster 3 in another. Ranking by cell
    count at least makes the id mean the same *kind* of thing everywhere: 1 is always the
    sample's largest cluster.

    Ties break on the original numeric label rather than being left to sort order, so two
    clusters of equal size do not swap ids between renders of the same data.

    Note these ids are this deck's own. cluster_report labels its panels with the raw
    leiden ids, so the two decks disagree on cluster names by design — the caption on
    each slide says so.
    """
    counts = labels.value_counts()
    return sorted(counts.index, key=lambda level: (-counts[level], int(level)))


def cluster_colors(levels):
    """level -> colour, matching cluster_report's palette so a cluster keeps its colour.

    tab10 below 11 clusters, tab20 above: tab20 is ten dark/light *pairs*, so a 2-cluster
    panel drawn from it is navy against pale blue. tab10's first two are blue and orange.
    Past 20 the palette cycles, which the numeric x labels compensate for.
    """
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("tab10" if len(levels) <= 10 else "tab20")
    return {level: cmap(i % cmap.N) for i, level in enumerate(levels)}


def style_axes(ax):
    """Shared framing: drop the top/right frame, shrink the labels to slide size."""
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
    ax.yaxis.label.set_size(7)


def point_size(ax, n_cells, coverage=0.35):
    """Marker area (pt²) that lets n_cells cover `coverage` of these axes, once.

    A fixed size cannot serve a cohort whose samples differ tenfold in cell count: at s=3
    a 20k-cell sample reads well but a 200k-cell one is a solid mat. Taking the axes' own
    area covers both — get_position() is the pre-tight_layout fraction of the figure,
    close enough for a marker size. 72 pt to the inch, squared, converts inches² to the
    pt² units scatter's `s` is in.
    """
    w, h = ax.get_figure().get_size_inches()
    pos = ax.get_position()
    area_pt2 = (pos.width * w) * (pos.height * h) * 72 ** 2
    return float(np.clip(coverage * area_pt2 / n_cells, 0.5, 6.0))


# The renumbering, fixed once per sample here rather than recomputed inside each plot, so
# the UMAP, the correlation heatmap, and the violins cannot disagree about which cluster
# is 1. LEVELS holds the original leiden labels in size order — position i is cluster
# i + 1 everywhere.
LEVELS = {s: size_ranked(samples[s][f"leiden_res_{CHOSEN[s]:.2f}"]) for s in SAMPLES}
COLORS = {s: cluster_colors(LEVELS[s]) for s in SAMPLES}


def cluster_centroids(sample):
    """Per-cluster centroids (clusters x genes), rows in size-rank order.

    Follows the sammy_r21 / PNAS atlas pseudobulk (Seurat AverageExpression + ln(avg + 1)):
    normalize each cell to CP10K, average the *linear* CP10K over the cells in a cluster,
    then log1p that average — mean-then-log, not log-then-mean, since ln is nonlinear and
    the two differ (up to 1.8 on this data). Built from the raw counts in layers["counts"]
    (ground truth), which cluster_sdata stashes before normalizing, rather than expm1(X),
    which round-trips the log transform.

    The CP10K target itself does not affect the numbers on this slide: a uniform per-cell
    scale factor leaves the gene ranks within a centroid untouched, so the within-sample
    Spearman is identical (to 1e-7) under any target_sum. It matters for comparability
    only — cluster_sdata's normalize_total takes no target_sum, and its default is not a
    constant but the median pre-normalization total, which is 226 for one of these samples
    and 198 for the other. Centroids built that way are on a per-sample scale and could not
    be compared across samples or against an external atlas; CP10K can.

    This is the one place the deck touches a count matrix. It is read, reduced to
    n_clusters rows, and dropped before the next sample is opened — a cohort's worth of
    matrices held at once would be tens of GB, while the centroids are a few thousand
    floats per cluster.
    """
    store = zarr.open(f"{zarr_paths[sample]}/tables/table", mode="r")
    counts = ad.io.read_elem(store["layers"]["counts"])
    genes = ad.io.read_elem(store["var"]).index

    # CP10K. Every cell is past cluster_sdata's min_counts=10 cut, so no total is zero and
    # the division is safe. Scaling by a diagonal keeps a sparse matrix sparse; a dense
    # broadcast would materialize the whole thing.
    totals = np.asarray(counts.sum(axis=1)).ravel()
    scale = 1e4 / totals
    cp10k = sp.diags(scale) @ counts if sp.issparse(counts) else counts * scale[:, None]

    key = f"leiden_res_{CHOSEN[sample]:.2f}"
    labels = samples[sample][key].to_numpy()

    rows = []
    for level in LEVELS[sample]:
        cells = np.flatnonzero(labels == level)
        # np.asarray().ravel() because a sparse .mean(axis=0) returns a 1 x n np.matrix,
        # while a dense one returns a 1-D array — this normalizes both. log1p AFTER the
        # mean is the whole point of the recipe.
        rows.append(np.log1p(np.asarray(cp10k[cells].mean(axis=0)).ravel()))

    del counts, cp10k
    gc.collect()
    # Index is the size-ranked id, 1 = largest, matching the UMAP and violin labels.
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, index=range(1, len(LEVELS[sample]) + 1), columns=genes)


def rank_corr(centroids):
    """Spearman r between every pair of centroid rows.

    Spearman = Pearson of gene ranks: rank each centroid across genes, then correlate.
    Rank-based rather than Pearson on the values because a targeted panel's centroids are
    dominated by a few very high-expressing genes — those set a Pearson r almost on their
    own, while ranks weight the whole panel.
    """
    ranked = np.vstack([rankdata(v) for v in centroids.to_numpy()])
    return np.corrcoef(ranked)


def dendrogram_order(values):
    """Leaf order of an average-linkage tree on 1 - r, as indices into `values`.

    squareform wants a condensed vector and rejects any asymmetry or nonzero diagonal, so
    the diagonal is zeroed explicitly: 1 - r leaves it at ~1e-16 rather than exactly 0 and
    squareform raises on that. checks=False would skip the validation but also skip
    catching a genuinely malformed matrix, so the diagonal is fixed instead.
    """
    if len(values) <= 2:
        # linkage needs at least 3 observations to build a tree worth ordering; with 1 or
        # 2 clusters the incoming order is already the only sensible one.
        return np.arange(len(values))
    distance = 1 - values
    np.fill_diagonal(distance, 0.0)
    return leaves_list(linkage(squareform(distance, checks=False), method="average"))


# Centroids, their correlation, and the dendrogram order, computed once per sample here
# rather than inside a slide function. Both the heatmap and the dendrogram-ordered UMAP
# need the ordering, and X is by far the most expensive thing this deck reads — computing
# it per slide would read every count matrix twice.
#
# ORDER[s] indexes into size-rank positions: ORDER[s][p] is the size-rank position of the
# cluster that sits at dendrogram position p. DENDRO_LEVELS[s] resolves that to the
# original leiden labels, so position p is dendrogram cluster p + 1.
CORR, ORDER, DENDRO_LEVELS = {}, {}, {}
for s in SAMPLES:
    CORR[s] = rank_corr(cluster_centroids(s))
    ORDER[s] = dendrogram_order(CORR[s])
    DENDRO_LEVELS[s] = [LEVELS[s][i] for i in ORDER[s]]

DENDRO_COLORS = {s: cluster_colors(DENDRO_LEVELS[s]) for s in SAMPLES}


def centroid_correlation(sample, numbering):
    """One slide's figure: cluster-by-cluster Spearman correlation of centroids.

    Self-self, so the diagonal is 1 by construction and carries no information. The colour
    scale is set from the OFF-diagonal values alone: including the diagonal pins the top
    of the ramp at 1.0 and squashes every real comparison — which on a targeted panel all
    sit high and close together — into the top slice of the colormap.

    Rows and columns are ordered by hierarchical clustering, symmetrically, so the matrix
    stays symmetric and transcriptionally similar clusters sit adjacent as blocks. Only
    the TICKS differ between the two numberings — the matrix itself is identical, drawn in
    dendrogram order both times, so the two slides can be read against each other cell for
    cell.

    numbering="size"    ticks are the size-ranked ids, so they read out of sequence
                        (dendrogram order applied to size-ranked names).
    numbering="dendro"  ticks are the new ids, which read 1..n by construction — that
                        numbering IS this ordering.
    """
    order = ORDER[sample]
    values = CORR[sample][np.ix_(order, order)]
    if numbering == "size":
        # order[p] is a 0-based size-rank position; +1 makes it the printed size id.
        ids = [int(p) + 1 for p in order]
    else:
        ids = list(range(1, len(order) + 1))

    off_diagonal = values[~np.eye(len(ids), dtype=bool)]
    vmin, vmax = float(off_diagonal.min()), float(off_diagonal.max())

    # Blank the diagonal rather than drawing it. It is 1.0 by construction, above the
    # scale's top, so it renders in the same saturated colour as the highest real pair —
    # here 0.97 and 1.00 come out identical yellow while being a meaningful step apart.
    # Grey says "not a comparison" and leaves the ramp entirely to the off-diagonal.
    masked = values.copy()
    np.fill_diagonal(masked, np.nan)

    cmap = plt.get_cmap("viridis").copy()
    cmap.set_bad("#e8e8e8")

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(FIGSIZE[1], FIGSIZE[1]))
    image = ax.imshow(masked, cmap=cmap, vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax)

    ticks = range(len(ids))
    ax.set_xticks(ticks, [str(c) for c in ids], fontsize=6)
    ax.set_yticks(ticks, [str(c) for c in ids], fontsize=6)
    ax.set_xlabel("Cluster", size=7)
    ax.set_ylabel("Cluster", size=7)

    # Print the numbers while they still fit. Past ~12 clusters the cells are too small
    # for two decimals and the colour alone has to carry it.
    if len(ids) <= 12:
        for i in range(len(ids)):
            for j in range(len(ids)):
                if i == j:
                    continue  # blanked above; a printed 1.00 would only re-clutter it
                # Threshold on the colour, not the value: mid-viridis is light enough that
                # black reads better, and the ramp is stretched to the off-diagonal range.
                shade = (values[i, j] - vmin) / (vmax - vmin) if vmax > vmin else 0.5
                ax.text(j, i, f"{values[i, j]:.2f}", ha="center", va="center",
                        fontsize=5, color="white" if shade < 0.5 else "black")

    cbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, fraction=0.045, pad=0.02)
    cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
    cbar.set_label("Spearman r", size=7)

    label = "size-ranked ids" if numbering == "size" else "dendrogram-ordered ids"
    fig.suptitle(f"{sample} · {len(ids)} clusters · {label}", fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)


def umap_clusters(sample, levels, colors):
    """One slide's figure: this sample's UMAP, coloured by one of the two numberings.

    `levels` is the original leiden labels in the order the numbering assigns — position
    i is cluster i + 1 — and `colors` maps those labels to their colour. Passing both in
    rather than reading a global keeps the size-ranked and dendrogram-ordered versions of
    this plot on one code path, so they cannot drift apart in styling.

    Labels are drawn on the clusters rather than in a legend: past ~10 clusters a legend
    eats the panel, and tab20 has to cycle anyway — the on-data number is what actually
    identifies a cluster, so colour only has to separate neighbours.

    Clusters are drawn in the order given, so for the size-ranked numbering the small ones
    land on top. The reverse buries a 300-cell cluster under a 16,000-cell one wherever
    they overlap.
    """
    d = samples[sample]
    key = f"leiden_res_{CHOSEN[sample]:.2f}"

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(FIGSIZE[0] * 0.6, FIGSIZE[1]))
    size = point_size(ax, len(d))

    for level in levels:
        cells = d[d[key] == level]
        ax.scatter(cells["umap_1"], cells["umap_2"], s=size, color=colors[level],
                   alpha=1.0, edgecolors="none", rasterized=True)

    for i, level in enumerate(levels):
        cells = d[d[key] == level]
        # The median, not the mean: a cluster split across two lobes of the embedding
        # puts its mean in the empty space between them, where the label sits on no cells
        # at all. The median lands inside one of the lobes.
        ax.text(
            cells["umap_1"].median(), cells["umap_2"].median(), str(i + 1),
            fontsize=7, weight="bold", ha="center", va="center",
            # White outline so the number stays legible on both the dark and the light
            # end of the palette.
            path_effects=[patheffects.withStroke(linewidth=2, foreground="white")],
        )

    # UMAP axes carry no interpretable units — drop the frame entirely.
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.spines[["top", "right", "bottom", "left"]].set_visible(False)
    fig.suptitle(f"{sample} · {len(d):,} cells · {len(levels)} clusters", fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)


def qc_violins(sample, levels, colors):
    """One slide's figure: this sample's per-cell QC, one violin per cluster per metric.

    Takes `levels` and `colors` the same way umap_clusters does — the original leiden
    labels in the order the numbering assigns, so position i is cluster i + 1 — rather
    than reading a global, so the violins and the UMAP cannot end up on different
    numberings by accident.

    Metrics stack in rows over a shared cluster axis, so a cluster reads straight down
    the slide across all of them — a grid would repeat the cluster labels once per metric
    and halve the width each gets. The point of the slide is spotting the cluster that is
    a QC artefact rather than a cell type: low transcripts and genes together, or a
    negative-control fraction that stands off the rest.
    """
    d = samples[sample]
    key = f"leiden_res_{CHOSEN[sample]:.2f}"
    groups = {level: d[d[key] == level] for level in levels}

    metrics = [(c, label, log) for c, label, log in QC_COLUMNS if c in d.columns]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(metrics), 1, figsize=FIGSIZE, sharex=True, squeeze=False)

    for ax, (col, label, log) in zip(axes.ravel(), metrics):
        series = [groups[level][col].to_numpy() for level in levels]
        if log:
            # Guard the transform: cell_area can be 0 for a degenerate segmentation, and
            # log10(0) is -inf, which makes the KDE fit fail outright.
            series = [v[v > 0] for v in series]
            series = [np.log10(v) for v in series]

        # A violin needs a KDE, and a KDE needs spread: a cluster of one cell, or one
        # where every cell has the same value (pct_control is exactly 0 for whole
        # clusters), makes gaussian_kde raise on a singular covariance and would take the
        # whole panel down. Those positions get their median dot alone — the cluster
        # still appears on the axis rather than silently vanishing.
        drawable = [i for i, v in enumerate(series) if len(np.unique(v)) > 1]
        if drawable:
            parts = ax.violinplot(
                [series[i] for i in drawable],
                positions=[i + 1 for i in drawable],
                showextrema=False, widths=0.8,
            )
            for body, i in zip(parts["bodies"], drawable):
                body.set_facecolor(colors[levels[i]])
                body.set_alpha(0.8)

        # The median marker. Drawn separately rather than via showmedians so it reads as
        # one consistent point across every cluster, including the ones with no violin.
        medians = [np.median(v) if len(v) else np.nan for v in series]
        ax.scatter(range(1, len(levels) + 1), medians, s=6, color="black", zorder=3)

        ax.set_ylabel(label)
        if log:
            # Ticks at whole decades, labelled with the linear value they stand for, so
            # the axis reads in transcripts and µm² rather than in exponents.
            lo, hi = ax.get_ylim()
            decades = np.arange(np.floor(lo), np.ceil(hi) + 1)
            ax.set_yticks(decades)
            ax.set_yticklabels([f"{10 ** dec:,.0f}" for dec in decades])
            # Restore the limits set_yticks just widened. Autoscale is still live here, so
            # matplotlib expands the view to fit the outermost tick — the floor/ceil
            # rounding then pushes a 100-10,000 distribution out onto a 1-100,000 axis and
            # flattens every violin into a horizontal smear.
            ax.set_ylim(lo, hi)
        style_axes(ax)

    # Cluster sizes on the shared axis rather than in a caption: a narrow violin means
    # something different at n=40 than at n=4,000, and that is the first thing to check
    # on a cluster that looks like an outlier.
    bottom = axes.ravel()[-1]
    bottom.set_xticks(range(1, len(levels) + 1))
    bottom.set_xticklabels(
        [f"{i + 1}\nn={len(groups[level]):,}" for i, level in enumerate(levels)], fontsize=5
    )
    bottom.set_xlabel(f"Cluster (leiden resolution {CHOSEN[sample]:g})", size=7)

    fig.suptitle(f"{sample} · {len(d):,} cells · {len(levels)} clusters", fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)
```

```{python}
# One `# <sample>` section per sample, driven by SAMPLES rather than a hardcoded block
# each: the cohort changes, and a hardcoded list silently omits a new sample while
# raising KeyError on a removed one.
#
# The headings are emitted with display(Markdown(...)) from inside an ORDINARY cell, NOT
# under `output: asis`. Under asis everything a cell displays concatenates into one raw
# markdown stream: the figure lands between the blocks and leaves the next heading not
# starting its own line, so pandoc prints a literal "## ..." as text and drops the image
# entirely. display(Markdown) does not hit it — each call emits its own complete block,
# and qc_violins ends with plt.show() so the figure lands between them.
for sample in SAMPLES:
    display(Markdown(f"# {sample}"))

    # The UMAP comes first: it establishes what each cluster number and colour refers to,
    # which the violin slide then reads against.
    display(Markdown("## Clusters on the UMAP — size-ranked ids"))
    display(Markdown(
        "Cells in UMAP coordinates, coloured by cluster at this sample's Leiden "
        "resolution. Clusters are renumbered 1-n by descending cell count, so cluster 1 "
        "is the largest — these ids are this deck's own and do not match the raw Leiden "
        "labels cluster_report uses. Each number sits at its cluster's median position."
    ))
    try:
        umap_clusters(sample, LEVELS[sample], COLORS[sample])
    except Exception:
        display(Markdown(f"```\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n```"))

    display(Markdown("## Cluster centroid correlation — size-ranked ids"))
    display(Markdown(
        "Spearman correlation between every pair of cluster centroids within this "
        "sample, across all genes. Centroids are CP10K pseudobulk, averaged linearly "
        "over each cluster's cells and then log1p'd. Rows and columns are ordered by "
        "hierarchical clustering, so similar clusters sit adjacent as blocks — the "
        "size-ranked ticks therefore read out of numeric sequence. The diagonal is 1 by "
        "construction and is left blank, so the colour scale covers the off-diagonal "
        "values only. High off-diagonal pairs are clusters the chosen resolution split "
        "that are transcriptionally near-identical."
    ))
    try:
        centroid_correlation(sample, "size")
    except Exception:
        display(Markdown(f"```\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n```"))

    display(Markdown("## Cluster centroid correlation — dendrogram-ordered ids"))
    display(Markdown(
        "The same matrix as the previous slide, cell for cell — only the tick labels "
        "differ. Clusters are renumbered 1-n along the dendrogram order, so the ticks "
        "now read in sequence and adjacent numbers are transcriptionally adjacent. The "
        "mapping is "
        + ", ".join(f"{p + 1}←{int(ORDER[sample][p]) + 1}" for p in range(len(ORDER[sample])))
        + " (dendrogram←size)."
    ))
    try:
        centroid_correlation(sample, "dendro")
    except Exception:
        display(Markdown(f"```\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n```"))

    # The dendrogram-ordered UMAP follows the heatmaps, since they are what define this
    # numbering — reading it before the matrix that produced it would be backwards.
    display(Markdown("## Clusters on the UMAP — dendrogram-ordered ids"))
    display(Markdown(
        "The same cells and the same clusters as the first UMAP, carrying the "
        "dendrogram-ordered ids from the heatmap above, so adjacent numbers are "
        "transcriptionally adjacent. Colours follow the new numbering, so a given "
        "cluster is not the same colour here as on the size-ranked UMAP — the number "
        "identifies it, not the colour."
    ))
    try:
        umap_clusters(sample, DENDRO_LEVELS[sample], DENDRO_COLORS[sample])
    except Exception:
        display(Markdown(f"```\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n```"))

    display(Markdown("## Per-cell QC by cluster — dendrogram-ordered ids"))
    display(Markdown(
        "Per-cell QC distributions, one violin per cluster, at this sample's Leiden "
        "resolution. Clusters carry the dendrogram-ordered ids and colours, matching the "
        "heatmap and UMAP above, so adjacent violins are transcriptionally adjacent. "
        "Transcripts, genes, and cell area are on log axes; "
        "the black dot is each cluster's median. A cluster with no violin had too little "
        "spread to fit a density — its median is still plotted."
    ))
    try:
        qc_violins(sample, DENDRO_LEVELS[sample], DENDRO_COLORS[sample])
    except Exception:
        display(Markdown(f"```\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n```"))
```
